correctness.rationale: The cycle has all 27 cyclic triples once. A nine-mark solution must partition the 27 linear triple starts into three-start consecutive intervals; covering start 1 with full capacity forces mark 3 and induction forces 3,6,…,27 (one-based). This marks cyclic residue r=c+2 mod 3. In residues 0,1,2 the omitted bigram respectively is 02, 01, 12, with start residues 1,2,0, so both coordinates avoid the marks, including any repeated unmarked suffix. Independently computed occurrence-union bitmasks for every length in every one of the 27 cuts give exactly one missed factor with these nine marks, and adding one position in that factor hits every factor. Analytically, any factor longer than three has a unique triple suboccurrence, so hitting all triples already hits all such factors. This proves both minima exactly ten and both quantifiers over the given instance.
residual_risks: Linear unfoldings as specified; not a claim about all ternary cycles, circular attractors, or nonexistence of some favorable cycle.

evidence: Theorem 29 gives favorable Lyndon-generated sequences for prime orders; it is existential, while the all-sequences question is stated separately. The binary order-four profile has at least eight optimal cuts per cycle.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The prime-order existence result, including order three, is logically consistent with the explicit counterexample to universality. The binary profile cannot be specialized to a ternary order-three cycle.

evidence: Whittington's example fails at one ternary order-three unfolding but has a favorable alternative of the same cycle. The frozen cycle has universal failure at nine and uses the ordinary inclusive 3-attractor, not just the exact-length sharp criterion.
Uniqueness of the triples makes full and 3-attractor requirements equivalent here once the shorter factors are hit.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Being favorable for at least one cut is invariant under rotation and alphabet relabelling (also reversal when all cuts are taken). Thus the prior bad unfolding of a cycle with a good unfolding cannot be this witness in equivalent notation. The lower bound using exact-length factors alone is not the obstruction at shorter lengths.

The elementary lower bound and a single bad unfolding are prior context; the distinct claim is that all unfoldings of one cyclic ternary order-three word fail the target nine. The primary text explicitly separates this all-cycles question from the existence of some favorable cycle and has a favorable cut for its own illustrative cycle. The closest inspected Resultary profile is binary order four and has favorable cuts, not this witness.

value.rationale: The explicit witness rejects a universal rotation fix (not just a single bad linear representation); it separates forcing the exact-length factors from hitting all shorter factors. The modest finite certificate resolves a natural quantifier in the de Bruijn attractor question and gives a structural obstruction through the forced residue class.
residual_risks: No general extremal bound or progress on the separate existence conjecture is asserted.
